correctness.rationale: The Solomon–Tits theorem and subspace Möbius number give a simply connected two-dimensional wedge of q^6 spheres. The unique subfield F_(q^2) identifies all nontrivial Singer stabilizers; ranks cannot permute in a simplex, so fixed sets are exactly q^2+1 isolated rank-two vertices for each of q nonidentity subgroup elements. Armstrong gives π1=C_(q²+1), Burnside Euler gives χ=q³−q²+1, and free top chains plus UCT yield integral homology/cohomology. Exact independently enumerated quotient-chain Smith calculations pass for q=2 and3; they are not used as the all-q proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Drudge is broader in dimension for orbit counts and directly covers the component concerning possible flat stabilizers and the exceptional projective line spread; it does not compute flag-complex ordinary orbit topology. Arone–Dwyer addresses equivariant homology approximations and Borel models for a different action, not a result dominating the stated integral quotient calculation.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete integral homology and π1 classification of an infinite geometric orbit family. Rank four is the first projective building with an intermediate-field Singer stabilizer and nonfree flag action; the answer reveals arbitrarily large cyclic H1/H2-cohomology torsion in quotients of integral sphere wedges and a closed top-homology rank q²(q−1). The precise object/invariants are canonical, not a tuned finite parameter slice.
